entries.statement: A STITCHED series (more than one component) is owned by the stitcher: a plain resolve refreshes only AFL's episode rows within the translated numbering range and leaves the aggregate to the next stitch run, so it cannot collapse back to one season.

entries.statement: Episode rows MERGE, never full-replace: AFL owns only its own numbering range, so the writer deletes rows <= the TRANSLATED page max and re-inserts; rows beyond it (AFG-filled tails, curated specials) survive a page refresh.
entries.notes: Boundary uses the translated max because AFL numbering can sit +N of ours past an order-only insert (Ryuusui); deleting to the source-space max would eat rows the translation does not refill.

entries.statement: Stale-zone healing: when translation SHRINKS the range (our max < source max), rows stranded in (ourMax, sourceMax] are pre-translation leftovers wearing shifted titles and are purged — stale wrong data never self-heals; an AFG tail re-extends.

Sparse-classification hold: a non-RELEASING show whose AFL page classifies fewer than 60% of AniList's episode total is held (count_mismatch {sparse}) rather than published as a misleading strip; it returns automatically once classification grows past the bar.

entries.statement: A gap of more than 12 episodes between AniList's aired count and AFL's classified max files an informational count_mismatch flag; resolve proceeds (a season of natural lag is noise).

entries.statement: aired_episodes for a single-season series = AniList nextAiringEpisode-1 when airing, else AniList episodes, else AFL's max; total_episodes = AniList episodes; then the episode floor and community cap apply.
Every resolve upserts a baseline component row (season_order 1, episodes 1..total, afl_offset 0); the stitcher replaces baselines with full chains for multi-season series.
